metaDesc: A 2-day Samut Prakan seafood plan near Bangkok: old-town Paknam eats, waterfront seafood joints, Bang Pu classics like Sala Sukjai, Moken and the fort restaurants, with times, prices and how to get there.

h1:
Samut Prakan Seafood Run
Paknam & Bang Pu in 2 Full Days
intro: Samut Prakan sits right at the mouth of the Chao Phraya, just a long ride down the BTS green line from Bangkok, which is exactly why city folk treat it as their easy day trip for fresh seafood. This plan eats its way through two days, starting with the old-school food stalls of Paknam market, moving on to waterfront seafood houses, then heading out to Bang Pu to eat slowly in the sea breeze. Every place here is genuinely open and locals keep coming back to them.

blocks.html: The best thing about eating seafood in Samut Prakan is how close it is. Paknam sits right at the end of the BTS green line, so you get off at Paknam station and just walk or hop on a songthaew. Bang Pu is a bit further out along the old Sukhumvit Road, reachable by car or by bus. The seafood here comes off the inner Gulf of Thailand and the fish piers around Mahachai and Samut Sakhon just across the way, so you get prawns, blue crab, shellfish and sea bass at prices easier on the wallet than restaurants in central Bangkok.

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: Most of the waterfront spots and Bang Pu restaurants open from late morning through evening, and a few close on weekdays or have a fixed day off each week. A quick call to check is the safest bet. Seafood prices rise and fall with the season and the size of the catch, so the figures in this article are rough estimates from recent reviews, handy for ballparking your budget.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Paknam: old-town eats + waterfront seafood

blocks.html: Day one stays in Paknam town. Eat your way through the morning market first, then close out with a waterfront seafood restaurant in the evening. Every stop is within walking distance or a short songthaew ride from Paknam BTS station.

items.activity: Get off at Paknam BTS, start at Paknam Market
items.note: An old market in the middle of town packed with longtime food stalls. You can wander and graze through breakfast for a good while, and fresh seafood is sold wholesale and retail in the same market.
A longtime Paknam shop making its own fish balls, open more than 60 years across three generations. Bouncy fish balls, clear broth, a bowl that runs in the low double digits of baht.

items.activity: Lim Damrong khanom jak & sweet sticky rice
items.note: A legendary Paknam shop, handed down through three generations over more than 100 years. The khanom jak is fragrant with coconut, easy to grab as a sweet snack for the road.

items.activity: Lunch break, stroll the Paknam waterfront and look across at Phra Samut Chedi
items.note: If you have time, take the ferry across to pay respects at Phra Samut Chedi. The crossing costs just a few baht.

items.activity: Rim Khuean Seafood, early dinner as it opens
items.note: 858 Mueang Samut Prakan, open 16:00-22:00. A longtime spot with open-air tables, food comes out fast, around 300 THB per person on average.

items.activity: Order fish-sauce-marinated raw prawns, steamed blue crab, horseshoe-crab roe salad, blue-crab papaya salad
items.note: The standout dishes at the waterfront spot. Finish with mango sticky rice, an evening meal in the river breeze.

blocks.title: If you want to switch up dinner
blocks.html: In Paknam town there's also Sompong Seafood, a big place open more than 20 years with both an air-conditioned room and an outdoor garden, around 250-500 THB per person. The dishes people order most are oyster omelette, steamed jumbo crab meat, and a hot mixed appetizer platter, a good call if you're with a bigger group.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Bang Pu: eat long in the sea breeze

blocks.html: Day two heads out toward Bang Pu, along the old Sukhumvit Road about 10-15 km from Paknam town. You can drive or take a bus/songthaew. Bang Pu is the inner Gulf of Thailand coast, home to the Bang Pu Recreation Center, the Sukta Pier, and a row of seaside seafood restaurants. The vibe is sea breeze all day, the kind of place you sit and eat for hours with no need to rush.

items.activity: Enter the Bang Pu Recreation Center, walk Sukta Pier, watch the seagulls
items.note: From late in the year into early the next, migrating seagulls flock here. Walk out along Sukta Pier over the sea and take in the view before lunch.

items.activity: Sala Sukjai, lunch on the pavilion jutting out over the sea
items.note: A Bang Pu classic, open roughly 10:00-20:00, with both an air-conditioned zone and breezy outdoor tables. Seafood dishes start in the low double digits, with standouts like fried sea bass with fish sauce, crab dip, and mixed-vegetable sour curry.

items.activity: Sip a drink and listen to the sea breeze, or join the evening ballroom dancing in high season
items.note: Sala Sukjai has a retro ballroom-dance floor at certain times, a particular charm of Bang Pu that has been around for ages.

items.activity: Moken, dinner by the sea at the river mouth
items.note: 888 Moo 3, Bang Pu subdistrict, open roughly 11:00-20:00 (Sat-Sun until 21:00), with live music. Standout dishes include steamed fish with lime, blue crab stir-fried with curry powder, and steamed razor clams with garlic, around 250-500 THB per person.

items.activity: Catch the sunset over the Gulf of Thailand before heading back
items.note: The Bang Pu side looks out over the inner Gulf, with lovely light in the evening. If you're driving back to Bangkok, avoiding rush hour makes the trip smoother.

blocks.html: A roundup of the seafood restaurants in this plan, ordered by how often locals and reviews mention them. Each one is good at something different, so pick based on whether you're heading to the Paknam side or Bang Pu.

items.name: Sala Sukjai (Bang Pu Recreation Center)
items.blurb: A classic on a pavilion jutting out over the sea, where you eat in the breeze and watch the seagulls, with a retro ballroom-dance floor at certain times. Homestyle seafood like fried sea bass with fish sauce, crab dip, and mixed-vegetable sour curry. The draw is the atmosphere and the seaside spot.
items.price: from low double digits THB; mains 300-450 THB

items.name: Moken
items.blurb: A seaside seafood restaurant at the mouth of the Gulf of Thailand, breezy all day with live music and bold, fresh flavors. The dishes people order most are steamed fish with lime, blue crab stir-fried with curry powder, steamed razor clams with garlic, and the local shrimp paste dishes.

items.name: Rim Khuean Seafood
items.blurb: A longtime spot in central Paknam with open-air tables and food that comes out fast, good for an evening get-together with friends. Standouts are fish-sauce-marinated raw prawns, prawns baked with glass noodles, steamed blue crab, horseshoe-crab roe salad, and blue-crab papaya salad.
items.price: around 300 THB per person on average

items.name: Sompong Seafood
items.blurb: A big seafood restaurant open more than 20 years, with both an air-conditioned room and an outdoor garden, good for a larger group or a banquet. Popular orders are oyster omelette, steamed jumbo crab meat, and a hot mixed appetizer platter.

items.name: Samosorn Thai Ruea Luang Mae Klong
items.blurb: An old restaurant inside Phra Chulachomklao Fort, right by the Paknam seafront with views over the river mouth. You can see HTMS Mae Klong and the disappearing guns, and pay respects at the statue of King Rama V, all in one place, ideal for pairing food with a bit of history.
items.meta: Phra Chula Fort, Suksawat Rd, Phra Samut Chedi · 10:00-22:00

items.name: Samosorn Phra Chula Seafood
items.blurb: Another spot in the Phra Chula Fort area, set by a canal with a shady, quiet feel, good for a lunch stop after walking the fort and museum.
items.meta: Phra Chula Fort, Phra Samut Chedi

items: Into Paknam — ride the BTS green line all the way to the end and get off at Paknam station. Paknam Market and the waterfront are within walking distance or a short songthaew ride.

To Bang Pu — from Paknam, take a bus or songthaew along the old Sukhumvit Road, or just drive, which is the easiest option with parking available. The Bang Pu Recreation Center is around the 37 km marker on Sukhumvit Road.
To Phra Chula Fort — it's on the Phra Samut Chedi side; cross by ferry from Paknam or drive around via Suksawat Road, a good fit with a day of history sightseeing.
Driving from Bangkok — take the expressway or Sukhumvit Road to Paknam, around 30-45 min outside rush hour, plus another 20-30 min on to Bang Pu.

blocks.title: Getting the most out of your seafood
blocks.html: Blue crab and prawns are freshest and best priced when the catch is plentiful. Ask the restaurant what's fresh today and order accordingly, you'll usually get both freshness and better value than ordering off the picture menu. Seaside spots get busy on Saturday and Sunday evenings, so if you want a table with a good view, go before late afternoon.

faq.q: Can I do a Samut Prakan seafood trip in a single day?
faq.a: Yes, if you pick one side. For example, stay in Paknam, eat the morning market then a waterfront spot in the evening; or head to Bang Pu for the whole day with lunch at Sala Sukjai and dinner at Moken. But if you want to eat both Paknam and Bang Pu without rushing, splitting it into 2 days is more relaxed.

faq.q: Can I get to Bang Pu by public transport?
faq.a: You can, though it's not as convenient as driving yourself. The easiest way is to take the BTS to Paknam, then a bus or songthaew along the old Sukhumvit Road into Bang Pu. If you're with a group, hiring a car or driving yourself is smoother since the restaurants are spread along the road.

faq.q: Is seafood in Samut Prakan expensive?
faq.a: It's noticeably cheaper than seafood restaurants in central Bangkok. The waterfront and Bang Pu spots average around 250-500 THB per person for a filling meal. If you go for big crab or large prawns, the price climbs with size and season, so ask the per-kilo price before ordering to budget more accurately.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Bang Pu?
faq.a: Late in the year into early the next (roughly November-March), when the weather is cool and it's seagull migration season at Sukta Pier. You can watch the birds and follow it with a seafood meal in one trip. The rainy season still works, but expect strong wind and frequent rain.

faq.q: Is there a seafood spot that combines sightseeing and eating in one place?
faq.a: Yes. We'd suggest Samosorn Thai Ruea Luang Mae Klong at Phra Chulachomklao Fort, where you can eat seafood by the Paknam seafront while seeing HTMS Mae Klong, the disappearing guns, and paying respects at the statue of King Rama V, all in the same area.
